newsitem.title: USA: "Hollywood Madam" ordered to trial next week.
newsitem.headline: "Hollywood Madam" ordered to trial next week.

text.p: Reputed Hollywood Madam Heidi Fleiss, who was sent to a drug rehabilitation clinic last week, was ordered by another judge on Monday to stand trial on pandering charges for a second time next week.

Fleiss, convicted in 1994 of three counts of pandering in connection with a high-priced prostitution ring she ran in Hollywood, was sentenced to three years in prison. But the conviction was reversed by a state appeals court this year because of improper jury conduct.
The same jury acquitted her of providing cocaine.

On Monday Judge Judith Champagne set her retrial date for Oct. 16, when she will again face a mandatory three-year term on the pandering charge. In addition to the state charges, Fleiss was awaiting sentencing on federal charges of tax evasion and money laundering.
That sentencing was postponed last week when a federal judge ordered Fleiss to enter a residential drug rehabilitation clinic after she admitted violating terms of her bail by using illegal drugs.

Fleiss, 30, told the judge last week that she had suffered a relapse and used the illegal drug methamphetamine as a result of intense pressure she had been under. She was allowed out of the Impact House clinic Monday to appear in court.

Wearing a stylish black suit with black stockings and high-heeled shoes, she told reporters afterwards: "I'm in recovery, I just hope for the best. It's just a very important programme I can focus on to help me deal with these issues the best I can."
Her lawyer Donald Marks told reporters she was confident of being acquitted this time. "We're convinced that if we have to try this case, she wouldn't be convicted."
